places.name: Detroit
places.connection: The city where Sixto Rodriguez lived and worked, featured prominently in the film.

places.name: Cape Town
places.connection: Key interviews and scenes were shot here, as it is central to the story of Rodriguez's popularity in South Africa.

places.name: Johannesburg
places.connection: Location for interviews and scenes depicting Rodriguez's impact in South Africa.

places.name: The Fox Theatre
places.connection: A notable venue in Detroit, relevant to the music scene depicted in the film.

places.name: Sixto Rodriguez's Home
places.connection: Rodriguez's long-term residence where he lived and worked as a manual laborer, unaware of his fame in South Africa. Featured prominently in the film.

places.name: The Old Miami Bar
places.connection: One of the bars where Rodriguez performed in his early career in Detroit, mentioned and depicted in the film.

places.name: Mabu Vinyl Record Store
places.connection: Owned by Stephen 'Sugar' Segerman, who initiated the search for Rodriguez. Featured as a key location where Rodriguez's music was discovered and cherished in South Africa.

places.name: GrandWest Arena
places.connection: One of the main venues where Rodriguez performed his triumphant comeback concerts in South Africa, shown extensively in the film.

places.name: Standard Bank Arena (formerly Ellis Park Arena)
places.connection: Another major venue where Rodriguez performed his comeback concerts in South Africa, featured in the film.

places.name: Table Mountain Viewpoint (Upper Cableway Station)
places.connection: Prominent establishing shots of Cape Town, symbolizing the city where Rodriguez's music found its unexpected fame.

places.name: Michigan Central Station Area
places.connection: Featured in establishing shots of Detroit, representing the industrial background and working-class life of Rodriguez.

places.name: Clifton Coastal Road (Victoria Road)
places.connection: Scenic driving shots along the beautiful Cape Town coastline, contrasting with Detroit's urban decay.

places.name: Egyptian Theatre (Sundance Premiere)
places.connection: Venue for the world premiere of 'Searching for Sugar Man' at the 2012 Sundance Film Festival.

places.name: Motown Museum (Hitsville U.S.A.)
places.connection: Represents the rich musical history of Detroit, the city where Rodriguez's career began, offering context to his artistic background. A pilgrimage site for music fans.

places.name: The Lickey Hill Tavern (now The Lickey Banker)
places.connection: Historic performance venue for Sixto Rodriguez during his brief UK tour in 1970, referenced in the film as part of his early career. A pilgrimage site for dedicated fans.

places.name: Sveriges Television (SVT) Headquarters
places.connection: Co-producer of the film. Likely involved in post-production, editing, and potentially interviews with director Malik Bendjelloul.

places.name: District Six Museum
places.connection: Represents the socio-political context of apartheid South Africa, where Rodriguez's music became an anthem of freedom and resistance, as explored in the film. A significant cultural landmark related to the film's themes.
